title: Colin Chapman Would Approve: This VHPK Elise Is the Lightest You’ll Ever See

body_markdown:
If you thought the original[Lotus Elise S1](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/hagerty-insider/car-profiles-hagerty-insider/why-the-series-1-lotus-exige-deserves-your-attention/) was stripped out and light, think again. The new VHPK from[Analogue Automotive](https://analogueautomotive.co.uk/) in the U.K. ditches the car’s passenger seat and adds carbon fiber to bring it in at a featherweight 1320 lbs.


What’s more, the VHPK moves the driver to the middle of the car for ideal weight distribution, replaces all the fiberglass body panels with carbon, and features forged alloy wheels and carbon-ceramic brakes. Full carbon wheels can be specified to shed another 24 pounds.


Inspiration for the VHPK came from the short-lived Autobytel Lotus Championship, which featured similar monoposto Elises battling on track in support of the British Touring Championship. As for the VHPK name, that can only stand for Very High Performance K-Series, as the car’s Rover engine has been bored out to 1.9 liters and filled with billet and forged internals to deliver 247 hp. That’s around 30 percent more than Lotus’ own VHPD engine used in the Elise Sport 190. A Quaife PG1 five-speed close-ratio transmission sends power to the rear wheels, unadulterated by traction control.


“Crucially, this ensures that the car’s powertrain retains its original character, authenticity and feel,” says Anologue Automotive. “The VHPK delivers exhilarating performance without a complete engine swap or the need for forced induction, keeping it closely aligned to the spirit of the original car.”


On the chassis side, the VHPK uses lightweight aluminium uprights and steering arms, as well as multi-way passive dampers. A fully active suspension system is also available to customers who want to go all-out on handling.


Analogue Automotive has just completed this first customer car of 35, and it’s finished in a throwback PK Purple with a matching Alcantara interior and gold exhaust tips. Buyers can opt for fully exposed carbon bodywork, a carbon hardtop, and an electric heating and air conditioning system so the VHPK can be used year-round.


Each of the 35 cars will be individually numbered and specified to its buyer’s wishes, with price from around $470,000 plus taxes. The VHPK might be light, but its price certainly isn’t.


Analogue Automotive
